- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often overcorrects downward; allow for slight upward bias to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model frequently overreacts with continued steep rise; cap forecast slope or introduce early mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops after a peak; add a small downward bias in the first 5–7 days post-peak.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is neutral or weak; apply a 2–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If true outcome shows a sharp reversal from high to low (e.g., >75 → <65), model often fails to recognize the turn; introduce a lagged correction rule: if 3-day moving average of true price drops, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment history when forecasting; always weight recent sentiment (last 3–5 days) as a multiplier to forecast adjustment (e.g., +0.1 to +0.3 if sentiment >0.2, -0.1 to -0.3 if sentiment < -0.2).
